name: POS v11: checkout over a minute faster
object: Shopify POS version 11, the rebuilt point-of-sale app, and the time it shaves off every in-store checkout
audience: retail merchants and the store staff who ring up busy, in-person sales lines all day
message: This video tells retail merchants that Shopify rebuilt POS from the ground up so staff can ring up a full cart over a minute faster, and lets a real merchant back that claim up.

moments.what: a voiceover opens over shots of a tablet POS stand in a boutique, calling POS v11 a ground-up rebuild of the selling engine staff run hundreds of times a day
moments.copy: POS v11 is a ground-up rebuild of the engine your staff run hundreds of times a day

moments.what: close-ups of the new checkout UI as the narrator lists specific speed-ups: adding a customer in a few taps with pre-filled details, tapping a saved discount code, and ringing a full cart through with fewer steps, landing on the claim that it's over a minute faster for heavy POS users; an on-screen label reads 'POS v11 in action'
moments.copy: adding customers in a few taps, discounts ready to tap, a streamlined checkout that's over a minute faster

moments.what: cut to a real staff member at Province of Canada talking to camera in the store, saying the new POS is night-and-day faster than before, that product search is much improved, and that one person can now roam the floor with an iPad while checkout still moves quickly
moments.copy: it's so much faster, night and day from when I started using the POS; search is really improved, which creates a better experience in store

moments.what: a closing montage of staff helping customers, wrapping a purchase and handing over a bag, ends on the Shopify bag logo with no further text

cta: there is no spoken line at the end; the video closes on the Shopify logo and lets the speed claim plus the merchant's on-camera praise make the case for upgrading to POS v11
why: Pairing a crisp, numbers-led claim (over a minute faster) with unscripted praise from a staffer who uses the product daily turns a software update into something a retailer can feel: shorter lines, happier customers. The UI close-ups make the speed concrete rather than abstract, and ending on the merchant's voice rather than a sales pitch makes the claim more credible.
